config.note: v42 counts more than 50 clearly changed full-resolution pixels as a visible effect, so small label changes (OsmAnd's search radius) are not mistaken for no progress. v41: the Skill reminder and file state that an empty search result needs INCREASE SEARCH RADIUS, not SHOW ON MAP or zooming. v40: with the Skill enabled, every step's user message restates the waypoint search terms (the system-prompt Skill alone was not followed). v39 keeps the goal turn plus the latest 19 executed turns in each request (an 88-step run hit the provider's prompt limit), stops when a block of 2-6 actions repeats three times in a row, and lets the OsmAnd Skill list each waypoint's search term. v38 allows ten unchanged Waits in a row (was five): a cold OsmAnd start after the snapshot restore showed its logo for over 40 s on the software-rendered emulator. v37 allows 60 s per typed word (was 10 s): OsmAnd searches on every character and one word exceeded 10 s on the software-rendered emulator. v36 bounds unchanged Wait actions separately (stop after five in a row) so a slow splash screen is not mistaken for a no-progress cycle; other actions keep the v29 cycle stop. v35 confirms each screen-recorder clip survives encoder start-up (1.5 s) before GUI actions resume and starts a new clip otherwise (observed: 'unable to configure video/avc codec ... err=-38'); agent behaviour unchanged from v34. v34 keeps the shared ADB server when android_env retries a timed-out command (its kill-server also ended the screen recorder) and adds an optional per-task Skill: instructions/skills/osmand_track.md for OsmAndTrack, written from a manual exploration that passed the official track matcher. evaluate_tasks.py --disable-skills runs the same code without it. v33 launches apps with a 30-second `am start -W` timeout: Android World's 5 seconds expired on a cold OsmAnd start, android_env then restarted the ADB server and that also ended the screen recorder. v32 replaces a recorder clip that ends early (polled each second, logged as RECORDING NOTE) and closes a host adb shell that does not return after SIGINT; agent behaviour unchanged from v31. v31 resolves Launch names like upstream Open-AutoGLM (case/spacing-insensitive; a translated non-Latin name resolves only when exactly one app is allowed) and stops on all-black screenshots as a rendering infrastructure error. v30 adds SimpleCalendarAddOneEvent (medium) and OsmAndTrack (hard) with visible completion rules and initial step/time budgets of about 2x and 1.5x their 17/60 reference steps, to be revised from learning trials; Calendar verifier rows are withheld from model inputs. v29 follows pinned Open-AutoGLM English contract and sourced Android World guidance. Long task recipes and Clock keypad Type exception withdrawn. Short visible goals, ordered native history, latest screenshot, checked GUI state and actual selected-control feedback. Bounded recorder readiness and observed EditText recognition repair recorded adapter faults. Scheduler stops at the first failed clean trial; repeated unchanged action cycles stop without forcing completion. Sixteen offline checks; live task-specific v20/v28 gates and unresolved Timer/Clipboard errors are in docs/WARMUP_RESULTS.md. Sources/slide mapping: docs/COURSE_AND_UPSTREAM_REVIEW.md.

data.goal: Save a track with waypoints Oberplanken, Liechtenstein, Malbun, Liechtenstein in the OsmAnd maps app in the same order as listed.

data:
The screen is the home screen with app icons. To start the task, I need to open the OsmAnd maps app. The app is not visible on the home screen, so I should use the Launch action to open it directly.


do(action="Launch", app="osmand")

The OsmAnd app is open and shows the map view. To start creating a track, I need to open the search to look for the first waypoint "Oberplanken, Liechtenstein". The Search button is the magnifier icon at [134,59,241,108].

do(action="Tap", element=[187,83])

The OsmAnd app is open and shows the map. To start creating a track, I need to open the search to look for the first waypoint "Oberplanken". The Search button is the magnifier icon at the top-left of the screen.

do(action="Tap", element=[187,83])

The search panel is open with the input field focused. I need to type the first waypoint name "Oberplanken" into the search field to find the place.


do(action="Type", text="Oberplanken")

The search result shows "Could not find anything: 5 mi" and offers to INCREASE SEARCH RADIUS. To find the place, I should tap the "INCREASE SEARCH RADIUS" button to expand the search area.

do(action="Tap", element=[499,335])

The search still shows "Could not find anything: 10 mi" with the "INCREASE SEARCH RADIUS" button available. I should tap that button again to expand the search further.

do(action="Tap", element=[499,335])

The search still shows "Could not find anything: 20 mi" with the "INCREASE SEARCH RADIUS" button. I should tap the "INCREASE SEARCH RADIUS" button again to expand the search further.

do(action="Tap", element=[499,335])

The search now shows a result for "Oberplanken" (Hamlet) at 3299 mi. I should tap the "Oberplanken" row to open its place card and then proceed to add it to the route.

do(action="Tap", element=[499,219])

The place card for "Oberplanken" is open. To add this waypoint to the route, I should tap the "Add" button at the bottom of the card.

The "Add Favorite" screen is open with the name "Oberplanken" filled in. To add this as a waypoint, I should tap the "Save" button at the bottom right.
